html:
Japan's population peaked at about 128 million around 2008 and has fallen every year since 2011. Japan was the first large rich country to shrink this way, and it is the oldest society on earth.

Births had been low since the 1970s. People married later and had fewer children, and the fertility rate fell to around 1.3, far below the 2.1 needed to keep numbers steady. People also lived longer than almost anywhere else. By the 2020s nearly three in ten Japanese were 65 or over, and the population had dropped below 124 million.

The effects reach everywhere: empty houses in the countryside, closed schools, too few workers, and the cost of pensions and health care resting on fewer people. Japan long kept immigration low, but it has lately let in more foreign workers.

A century ago Japan sent people out, to Hawaii and Brazil. South Korea, Taiwan, much of Europe and China, shaped by the one-child policy, are now on the same path.
sum: Japan's population peaked at about 128 million around 2008 and has fallen every year since 2011. Japan was the first large rich country to shrink this way, and it is the oldest society on earth.
